Coordinate Product Listings, Stock and Marketplace Orders

Thematic Area: Multichannel Commerce & Online Fulfilment Coordination

How might we manage supported marketplace listings, stock and orders through a shared process that fits the retailer’s online operations?

Background

An Indonesian healthy-food retailer and its prepared-food business use online sales channels alongside physical retail. The opportunity is to coordinate marketplace listings, stock and orders through a shared process.

The objective is to connect product information and availability with order intake, stock reservation, fulfilment and status updates. Shared records support more consistent online operations across supported channels.

Relevant startups offer multichannel commerce software, listing tools, inventory synchronisation and shipping integration. The collaboration focuses on the retailer’s Indonesian marketplace accounts and the operational handovers between channels and stores.

Significance of Problem

The key challenges are:

  • Inconsistent channel information: Separate listing and stock updates create outdated product and availability information.
  • Higher administrative effort: Repeated updates across channels consume staff time and complicate exception handling.
  • Unclear fulfilment handovers: Disconnected order and inventory records complicate preparation, dispatch and customer-status updates.

Existing Efforts

  • Available platform capability: A subscription multichannel platform consolidates listings, inventory, orders, shipping labels and sales reporting across supported marketplaces, including Shopee and Tokopedia.
  • First application: Connect selected marketplace accounts using representative products. Set up stock updates, order imports, reservations, cancellations and dispatch-status handling for the chosen channels.
  • Collaboration focus: Define the master stock record, update timing, product identifiers and exception ownership. Connect food-specific fulfilment requirements with account integration and compare processing effort and record consistency against the current workflow.

Potential Market Size

  • Indonesian e-commerce demand: Indonesian e-commerce GMV was projected at US$71 billion in 2025, growing by more than 14% from 2024. This measures merchandise value across product categories.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
